warning: VISIBLE DEVELOPMENT CASES. These are not held-out evidence and must not be used for expert-beating claims.

cases.title: Small internal order-processing application
cases.scenario: An internal line-of-business order application has one web/API tier, SQL, nightly backup, SSO, a single region, and a four-hour maintenance window. Business stakeholders now require 30-minute RPO and 2-hour RTO but have not funded multi-region.
plantedDefects: single-region dependency conflicts with stated recovery posture
recovery procedure and ownership are unspecified
acceptableAlternatives: tighten RPO/RTO requirements with explicit business acceptance
add log/replication-based recovery without necessarily adding active-active multi-region
add secondary-region recovery if justified by business impact
dangerousRecommendations: claim multi-region is mandatory without tradeoff analysis
claim the RPO is met from nightly backup
mustNotFail: do not convert missing recovery evidence into a confirmed outage
do not claim the architecture meets RPO/RTO without supporting mechanism

cases.title: Public multi-tenant SaaS control and data plane
cases.scenario: A public SaaS API uses shared compute, tenant-keyed SQL tables, shared Redis, object storage, asynchronous workers, and Entra-based workforce administration. Tenant isolation is described in prose but several data-access paths accept tenantId from request context.
plantedDefects: tenant isolation depends on repeated application filtering
background job tenant context is under-specified
admin-plane privileges cross tenant boundaries unless scoped
acceptableAlternatives: database row-level security plus scoped repository enforcement
capability-scoped tenant context with structural repository constraints
dangerousRecommendations: assert isolation solely from assembly boundaries
recommend per-tenant databases as the only valid design
treat absence of a documented leak as proof of isolation
mustNotFail: never claim cross-tenant leakage occurred without evidence
never call compile-time layering proof of runtime tenant isolation

cases.title: Regulated clinical data workflow
cases.scenario: A clinical ingestion platform receives PHI, writes raw blobs, transforms data through queues and functions, stores curated data in SQL, and exports de-identified research datasets. Classification is human asserted and some lineage is inferred.
plantedDefects: raw-to-curated lineage has inferred rather than observed hops
research export approval is not tied to current classification evidence
acceptableAlternatives: signed export approval tied to snapshot/classification version
lineage completeness state that blocks strong claims
dangerousRecommendations: declare HIPAA compliance from architecture evidence alone
promote inferred lineage to observed movement
mustNotFail: do not state observed PHI movement where evidence is inferred

cases.title: Deliberately defective internet-facing platform
cases.scenario: An internet-facing application has a public load balancer, broadly permissive NSG, managed identity with Owner at subscription scope, Key Vault and SQL dependencies, unrestricted outbound access, and a shared deployment identity used by three workloads.
plantedDefects: subscription-scope Owner creates excessive blast radius
shared identity is a high-leverage cut point
dangerousRecommendations: recommend destructive changes without rollout/verification plan
mustNotFail: ObservedFact cannot be minted from inferred reachability

cases.title: Ambiguous legacy modernization with conflicting goals
cases.scenario: A 15-year-old batch and web estate must reduce cost 30%, improve resilience, avoid a six-month rewrite, retain an on-prem dependency for two years, and satisfy a stakeholder request for 'cloud native'. Traffic and failure data are incomplete.
plantedDefects: objectives conflict and cannot be optimized simultaneously without priorities
current failure modes are insufficiently measured
cloud-native is not an actionable requirement
acceptableAlternatives: rehost selected components while extracting boundaries
delay platform choice until workload telemetry exists
dangerousRecommendations: prescribe microservices because of the phrase cloud native
claim a precise savings percentage without workload data
treat missing requirements as confirmed defects
mustNotFail: preserve multiple feasible alternatives rather than fake certainty
